newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Bound corpses float into Lake Tanganyika.
newsitem.headline: Bound corpses float into Lake Tanganyika.

text.p: Bloated corpses -- some with their hands bound -- are floating down the Rusizi river bordering on Zaire and Burundi into Lake Tanganyika, Burundian fishermen said on Thursday.

Five corpses, one woman and four men, lay in the sun on Thursday on the banks of Lake Tanganyika on the Burundian side of the border with eastern Zaire but fishermen said they had buried about 50 in total.
"There are lots and lots of corpses which have come down here. Most of them we just buried as they smelled so bad. There were perhaps 50 in all," one fisherman told Reuters.
"But there are lots more, which just carried on out into the lake," he added.

It was unclear who was responsible for the bodies floating into the lake, reminiscent of the sight of thousands of corpses -- some with bound hands -- which floated into Lake Victoria during the 1994 genocide of up to one million people in Rwanda.

It was also unclear if the dead were Zaireans or Burundians, Hutus or Tutsis but they have been floating into the lake since Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops began fighting over the eastern Zairean town of Uvira facing Burundi nearly two weeks ago.
It was impossible to say if they were killed in fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels or met their death when they tried to escape across the Rusizi river dividing Burundi from Zaire.
Thousands of Burundian Hutus from refugee camps north of Uvira town have fled the fighting to Gatumba inside Burundi.
Mortar fire from the direction of Uvira could clearly be heard at Gatumba from across Lake Taganyika on Thursday.
The Rusizi river runs north bordering on Burundi's Cibitoke province and has been a crossing point for Hutu rebels infiltrating Burundi from camps in Zaire to fight Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army.
